--- title: "Single-cell analysis with scranpy" subtitle: "A full QC-to-UMAP workflow on the Zeisel mouse brain dataset" --- This workflow follows the Zeisel et al. (2015) mouse brain dataset through quality control, normalization, feature selection, PCA, graph-based clustering, and UMAP. The analysis uses [`scranpy`](https://github.com/BiocPy/scranpy) with the full dataset (20,006 genes and 3,005 cells), and ggnomics for visualization. For a shorter introduction based on a subset of these cells, see [Getting started](getting-started.qmd). ::: {#c77c71bb .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import sys, pathlib sys.path.insert(0, str(pathlib.Path("_includes").resolve())) from setup import configure_warnings, ensure_matplotlib_initialized ensure_matplotlib_initialized() configure_warnings() import numpy as np import pandas as pd import scranpy import ggnomics as gg from plotnine import theme_bw, theme, labs, facet_wrap, scale_color_gradient, element_text, coord_fixed ``` ::: ## 1. Fetching and inspecting the SCE ::: {#35b25812 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} from data import load_zeisel_full sce = load_zeisel_full() sce.shape ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` (20006, 3005) ``` ::: ::: ::: {#765f6591 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} sce.get_assay_names() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` ['counts'] ``` ::: ::: ::: {#8ae871c6 .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} sce.get_column_data().get_column_names() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=4} ``` Names(['tissue', 'group #', 'total mRNA mol', 'well', 'sex', 'age', 'diameter', 'level1class', 'level2class']) ``` ::: ::: ::: {#f6991596 .cell execution_count=5} ``` {.python .cell-code} sce.get_alternative_experiment_names() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=5} ``` ['repeat', 'ERCC'] ``` ::: ::: The object contains two alternative experiments, `repeat` and `ERCC` (spike-in) features. The analysis below uses the main 20,006-gene assay. ## 2. A mitochondrial-gene mask from verified row names Mouse mitochondrial genes conventionally carry an `mt-` prefix. We derive the QC subset directly from the row names: ::: {#20ae899b .cell execution_count=6} ``` {.python .cell-code} row_names = sce.get_row_names() mito_genes = [g for g in row_names if str(g).lower().startswith("mt-")] len(mito_genes), mito_genes[:5] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=6} ``` (34, ['mt-Tl1', 'mt-Tn', 'mt-Tr', 'mt-Tq', 'mt-Ty']) ``` ::: ::: ::: {#2a743346 .cell execution_count=7} ``` {.python .cell-code} mito_mask = [str(g).lower().startswith("mt-") for g in row_names] ``` ::: ## 3. RNA QC metrics and cell filtering `scranpy.compute_rna_qc_metrics` computes per-cell library size (`sum`), number of detected genes (`detected`), and the mitochondrial proportion for the `mito` subset we just defined; `suggest_rna_qc_thresholds` derives outlier thresholds (median absolute deviation-based, scran-style) and `filter_rna_qc_metrics` turns them into a boolean keep-mask: ::: {#2b1e5c5e .cell execution_count=8} ``` {.python .cell-code} qc = scranpy.compute_rna_qc_metrics(sce.get_assay("counts"), subsets={"mito": mito_mask}) qc_df = qc.to_pandas() qc_df.describe() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=8} ```{=html}
sum detected subset_proportion.mito
count 3005.000000 3005.000000 3005.000000
mean 14954.194343 3776.732113 0.079560
std 9267.942024 1576.251293 0.060633
min 2574.000000 785.000000 0.000000
25% 8130.000000 2484.000000 0.039921
50% 12913.000000 3656.000000 0.066528
75% 19284.000000 4929.000000 0.102898
max 63505.000000 8167.000000 0.569549
``` ::: ::: ::: {#70b57122 .cell execution_count=9} ``` {.python .cell-code} thresholds = scranpy.suggest_rna_qc_thresholds(qc) keep = scranpy.filter_rna_qc_metrics(thresholds, qc) f"{keep.sum()} / {len(keep)} cells retained" ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=9} ``` '2874 / 3005 cells retained' ``` ::: ::: Plotting the QC metrics with `plot_coldata`, colored by whether a cell passed filtering: ::: {#4123f4e4 .cell execution_count=10} ``` {.python .cell-code} qc_plot_df = qc_df.copy() qc_plot_df["status"] = np.where(keep, "kept", "filtered") ( gg.plot_coldata(qc_plot_df, x="sum", y="detected", color_by="status") + labs(x="Library size (total counts)", y="Genes detected", title="Zeisel QC: library size vs. genes detected") + theme_bw() ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=10} ![](single-cell-scranpy_files/figure-html/cell-11-output-1.png){width=525 height=375} ::: ::: ## 4. Filtering, normalization, and size factors ::: {#cffeb41d .cell execution_count=11} ``` {.python .cell-code} filtered = sce[:, keep] cd = filtered.column_data for col in ("sum", "detected", "subset_proportion.mito"): cd = cd.set_column(col, qc_df.loc[keep, col].to_numpy()) filtered = filtered.set_column_data(cd) ``` ::: We pass the QC-derived library sizes explicitly as size factors, following the `normalize_rna_counts_se` interface. This also avoids a sparse-matrix shape issue in the installed scranpy version's default path: ::: {#da95cd96 .cell execution_count=12} ``` {.python .cell-code} size_factors = qc_df.loc[keep, "sum"].to_numpy() normed = scranpy.normalize_rna_counts_se(filtered, assay_type="counts", size_factors=size_factors) normed.get_assay_names() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=12} ``` ['counts', 'logcounts'] ``` ::: ::: ## 5. Variance modelling and highly variable genes ::: {#03d4b1e6 .cell execution_count=13} ``` {.python .cell-code} hvg_out = scranpy.choose_rna_hvgs_se(normed, assay_type="logcounts", top=4000) hvg_out.get_row_data().get_column_names() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=13} ``` Names(['featureType', 'mean', 'variance', 'fitted', 'residual', 'hvg']) ``` ::: ::: ::: {#788647dd .cell execution_count=14} ``` {.python .cell-code} hvg_df = hvg_out.get_row_data().to_pandas() # pandas treats a bool column as numeric, which would otherwise route this # straight into plot_coldata's continuous-color branch - map to a category # label explicitly so it's treated (and legended) as discrete. hvg_df["HVG status"] = hvg_df["hvg"].map({True: "highly variable", False: "other"}) ( gg.plot_coldata(hvg_df, x="mean", y="variance", color_by="HVG status") + labs(title="Mean-variance trend and chosen HVGs (scranpy)", x="Mean log-expression", y="Variance") + theme_bw() ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=14} ![](single-cell-scranpy_files/figure-html/cell-15-output-1.png){width=525 height=375} ::: ::: ## 6. PCA ::: {#ef5165ec .cell execution_count=15} ``` {.python .cell-code} hvg_flags = hvg_out.get_row_data().get_column("hvg") pca_out = scranpy.run_pca_se(hvg_out, features=hvg_flags, number=25, assay_type="logcounts") pca_out.get_reduced_dim_names() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=15} ``` ['PCA'] ``` ::: ::: ## 7. Nearest-neighbor graph, clustering, and UMAP `run_all_neighbor_steps_se` builds the shared-nearest-neighbor graph, runs graph-based (Leiden/Louvain-style multilevel) clustering, and computes both UMAP and t-SNE embeddings in one call: ::: {#9a75210e .cell execution_count=16} ``` {.python .cell-code} final = scranpy.run_all_neighbor_steps_se(pca_out, reddim_type="PCA") final.get_reduced_dim_names() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=16} ``` ['PCA', 'TSNE', 'UMAP'] ``` ::: ::: ::: {#dba401c3 .cell execution_count=17} ``` {.python .cell-code} final.get_column_data().get_column_names() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=17} ``` Names(['tissue', 'group #', 'total mRNA mol', 'well', 'sex', 'age', 'diameter', 'level1class', 'level2class', 'sum', 'detected', 'subset_proportion.mito', 'size_factor', 'clusters']) ``` ::: ::: ::: {#8e093e81 .cell execution_count=18} ``` {.python .cell-code} n_clusters = len(set(final.column_data.get_column("clusters"))) f"{n_clusters} graph-based clusters" ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=18} ``` '14 graph-based clusters' ``` ::: ::: `run_scranpy_pipeline_on_zeisel()` caches the processed SCE for later examples: ::: {#af7ccd2d .cell execution_count=19} ``` {.python .cell-code} from data import run_scranpy_pipeline_on_zeisel final = run_scranpy_pipeline_on_zeisel() ``` ::: ## 8. Plotting PCA and UMAP The same `plot_pca` and `plot_umap` functions can colour cells by cluster, the supplied cell-class annotation, a QC metric, or expression of a selected gene. The SCE adapter retrieves coordinates, annotations, and assays from their corresponding slots. ::: {#466aafb4 .cell execution_count=20} ``` {.python .cell-code} gg.plot_pca(final, color="clusters") + labs(title="PCA, colored by graph cluster") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=20} ![](single-cell-scranpy_files/figure-html/cell-21-output-1.png){width=525 height=375} ::: ::: ::: {#3ed375a9 .cell execution_count=21} ``` {.python .cell-code} gg.plot_umap(final, color="level1class") + labs(title="UMAP, colored by the original level1class annotation") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=21} ![](single-cell-scranpy_files/figure-html/cell-22-output-1.png){width=525 height=375} ::: ::: ::: {#b55a8150 .cell execution_count=22} ``` {.python .cell-code} gg.plot_umap(final, color="subset_proportion.mito") + scale_color_gradient(low="#dddddd", high="#B2182B") + labs(title="UMAP, colored by mitochondrial proportion") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=22} ![](single-cell-scranpy_files/figure-html/cell-23-output-1.png){width=525 height=375} ::: ::: ::: {#698a1520 .cell execution_count=23} ``` {.python .cell-code} gg.plot_umap(final, color="Gad2", layer="logcounts") + labs(title="UMAP, colored by Gad2 (interneuron marker) expression") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=23} ![](single-cell-scranpy_files/figure-html/cell-24-output-1.png){width=525 height=375} ::: ::: ### Point-order control `order=` draws selected categories last, which keeps small populations visible in dense embeddings: ::: {#9645c796 .cell execution_count=24} ``` {.python .cell-code} gg.plot_umap(final, color="level1class", order=["microglia", "endothelial-mural"]) + labs(title="UMAP with microglia/endothelial-mural drawn on top") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=24} ![](single-cell-scranpy_files/figure-html/cell-25-output-1.png){width=525 height=375} ::: ::: ### Faceting Use `facet_by=` when splitting an embedding by a metadata field. The plotting frame built by `plot_umap` contains only the coordinates and requested annotations, so a post-hoc `facet_wrap()` cannot refer to other SCE columns. ::: {#3a939a81 .cell execution_count=25} ``` {.python .cell-code} gg.plot_umap(final, color="clusters", facet_by="level1class") + theme_bw() + theme(legend_position="none") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=25} ![](single-cell-scranpy_files/figure-html/cell-26-output-1.png){width=525 height=375} ::: ::: ## 9. Descriptive comparison to the original annotation The graph-based clusters were calculated without using Zeisel's curated `level1class` or `level2class` labels. A cross-tabulation provides a useful descriptive comparison, although it is not a formal measure of clustering accuracy: ::: {#88c80a0a .cell execution_count=26} ``` {.python .cell-code} cd = final.column_data.to_pandas() comparison = pd.crosstab(cd["clusters"], cd["level1class"]) comparison ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=26} ```{=html}

Larger classes such as pyramidal neurons are distributed across several clusters, reflecting variation below the broad `level1class` annotation. ## 10. Expression violins and dot plots ::: {#49278f1e .cell execution_count=28} ``` {.python .cell-code} markers = ["Gfap", "Mog", "Gad2", "Snap25", "Aif1", "Cldn5"] gg.plot_expression(final, features=markers, group_by="level1class", layer="logcounts", log1p=False, ncol=2) + theme_bw() + theme(axis_text_x=element_text(rotation=45, hjust=1)) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=28} ![](single-cell-scranpy_files/figure-html/cell-29-output-1.png){width=525 height=375} ::: ::: ::: {#2767d0df .cell execution_count=29} ``` {.python .cell-code} gg.plot_dot(final, features=markers, group_by="level1class", layer="logcounts") + theme_bw() + theme(axis_text_x=element_text(rotation=45, hjust=1)) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=29} ![](single-cell-scranpy_files/figure-html/cell-30-output-1.png){width=525 height=375} ::: ::: ## 11. Heatmap ::: {#a7245e4d .cell execution_count=30} ``` {.python .cell-code} gg.plot_heatmap(final, features=markers, group_by="clusters", layer="logcounts", cluster_rows=True, cluster_cols=True) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=30} ![](single-cell-scranpy_files/figure-html/cell-31-output-1.png){width=525 height=375} ::: ::: ## 12. Converting to AnnData and reproducing the UMAP In the installed versions, PCA metadata are stored as a `biocutils.NamedList`, whereas `.to_anndata()` expects a mutable mapping for AnnData's `.uns`. The UMAP plot does not require those PCA metadata, so we omit them during conversion: ::: {#8a747a98 .cell execution_count=31} ``` {.python .cell-code} final_for_export = final.set_metadata({}) adata, _alt = final_for_export.to_anndata() adata.X = adata.layers["logcounts"] gg.plot_umap(adata, color="level1class") + labs(title="Same UMAP, plotted from the converted AnnData") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=31} ![](single-cell-scranpy_files/figure-html/cell-32-output-1.png){width=525 height=375} ::: ::: ## 13. A custom plotnine extension The returned UMAP can be extended with ordinary plotnine components. Here we fix the aspect ratio and add a caption from values calculated above: ::: {#f4bea97d .cell execution_count=32} ``` {.python .cell-code} gg.plot_umap(final, color="clusters") + coord_fixed() + labs( caption=f"{n_clusters} clusters, {final.shape[1]} cells passing QC out of {sce.shape[1]} total" ) + theme_bw() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=32} ![](single-cell-scranpy_files/figure-html/cell-33-output-1.png){width=525 height=375} ::: ::: ## Next * [Bulk RNA-seq](bulk-rnaseq.qmd) for PyDESeq2-based differential expression. * [Multimodal](multimodal.qmd) for RNA/ADT CITE-seq data. * [Specialized plots](specialized-plots.qmd) uses the processed Zeisel object for statistics, significance brackets, and palette examples.
